themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline average of 0.8 per week (up 433%), marking the sharpest emerging complaint type in CD201 and suggesting potential unlicensed retail operations or compliance issues may be accelerating.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.5)
This is the most recent statistically significant spike in the dataset
Suggests rapid emergence of unlicensed or non-compliant retail operations in Mott Haven/Melrose
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed cannabis retailers opening in the district faster than enforcement can keep pace?
What specific compliance violations are residents reporting (illegal signage, odor, traffic, loitering)?

themes_detail.label: Police Calls Increase 96%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 13 last week versus a baseline average of 6.6 per week (up 96%), indicating a possible safety or street disorder concern emerging in the past 7–10 days.
evidence: 13 non-emergency police complaints last week vs. 6.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (96% spike, z-score: 2.41)
Timing aligns with other emerging safety signals (vehicle noise up 137%, homeless assistance up 300%)
Converges with community board's repeated requests for homeless services, suggesting street conditions may be deteriorating
reporting_angles: What specific non-emergency incidents are spiking (trespassing, loitering, quality-of-life crimes)?
Is this spike correlated with the concurrent rise in homeless assistance complaints?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise and Homeless Concerns Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, vehicle noise complaints surged 137% (24 vs. 10.1 weekly average) and homeless person assistance complaints jumped 300% (11 vs. 2.8 weekly average), suggesting street disorder and unmet social service needs may be compounding.
evidence: Vehicle noise: 24 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 10.1 weekly average (137% spike, z-score: 2.54)
Homeless assistance: 11 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.03)
Community board has filed repeated budget requests for homeless services (unsolved multi-year pattern)
Convergence with non-emergency police spike suggests interconnected street-level crisis
reporting_angles: Are illegal street racing, modified vehicles, or commercial trucks causing the noise surge?
What is driving the spike in homeless service requests—visible encampments, lack of shelter capacity, new arrivals?
How are these two trends connected (if at all) and what is the city's response capacity?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints more than doubled 2 weeks ago to 7 versus a baseline of 2.8 per week (154% spike), possibly indicating mold, gas leaks, or ventilation failures affecting multiple buildings during spring conditions.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (154% spike, z-score: 2.72)
Timing suggests seasonal trigger (spring humidity, heating season end, or building maintenance failure)
Districtwide heat/hot water complaints remain very high at 2,051 over 90 days, indicating aging building stock vulnerable to systems failures
reporting_angles: Are specific buildings or blocks reporting clustered air quality issues?
Is this related to HVAC system shutdowns, inadequate ventilation in converted spaces, or mold from water damage?

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violation Anomaly
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violation complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 3 complaints versus a baseline of 0.1 per week (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69, the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset), though timing suggests the acute issue may have cooled; worth investigating what triggered the spike and whether conditions have normalized.
evidence: 3 park rules complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest anomaly in dataset)
Spike appears to have cooled in the intervening weeks (no current mention)
Community board has repeated requests for park improvements and building reconstruction, suggesting parks are stressed infrastructure
reporting_angles: What specific park rule violations occurred 3 weeks ago (illegal activity, unhoused encampment, vendor operations)?
Has Parks Department taken enforcement action, or have conditions returned to baseline?
